- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.4) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — especially after sharp spikes or drops; adjust for recent momentum.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects downward — suppress early correction peaks if sentiment remains bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — reduce forecast weight on recent extremes unless sentiment confirms trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates near the end of the forecast window — especially if sentiment is stable or slightly bullish — apply downward bias in final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is volatile or oscillating, model tends to smooth too much — allow for sharper transitions in forecast if sentiment shows momentum.
